assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE landscape 3:2 illustrated architectural book plate for The Chronicle: the civic chamber of Carthara's Three Seats. The two supplied images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY. Match their accomplished hand-drawn pen-and-ink etching, meticulous crosshatching, faded mineral watercolor, and intricate Mediterranean / Middle Eastern architecture on pale warm ivory paper. Entirely new interior, not a copy of the reference composition: broad vaulted civic chamber, richly carved horseshoe arches and mashrabiya screens, tiered galleries, muted teal glazed detail, pale stone and restrained brass water channels. At the far side, EXACTLY THREE equivalent official chairs sit at the SAME HEIGHT on ONE low shared dais, arranged beside one another, equal in scale; no towering throne or dominant fourth seat. These represent the fields, harbor, and garrison through modest material evidence on separate working tables: a grain measure, a small harbor chart with NO readable writing, and a plain closed military ledger. Small anonymous clerks bend over papers at lower desks; other tiny anonymous petitioners convey actual civic work rather than an imperial ceremony. The composition is mainly architectural, with clear three-chair silhouette. Morning filtered light, sober institutional wealth, elaborate ornament, potted greenery; no literal Roman Caesars, laurel crowns, modern office equipment, guns, holograms, or Roman state iconography. Muted terracotta, washed teal, brass ochre, warm charcoal. Fine delicate linework, visible paper grain, elegant illustrated novel / architectural travel folio, irregular outer edges dissolving into untouched warm ivory paper (#eee7d8), generous paper margins. No 3D rendering, no photorealism. No readable text, letters, captions, logos, watermarks, frames, or page mockup. Image only; website supplies captions.
assets.inspection: Inspected generated PNG: exactly three comparable chairs share one dais; grain measure, chart and closed ledger distinguish offices; anonymous clerks, richly etched civic architecture, no legible text.

assets.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Generate ONE square illustrated still-life plate for an epic novel. It is a plain walking staff approximately a person's height, with simple natural wood grain, a smooth worn handgrip and ONE short BLUNT metal ferrule capping its ground end. The TOP is plain rounded wood. Absolutely NO pointed tip, no blade, no spearhead at either end, no crystal, no magic, no glow, no horns, no ornate crown or weapon fittings. Do not write its name or any letters on it. Lean the full staff against a pale carved stone bench so both ends are visible, beside a practical worn travel satchel and two closed working notebooks with blank unlettered covers. A corner of carved screen, a restrained water channel, and potted greenery can place this ordinary travel equipment in the same sophisticated Mediterranean/Middle Eastern world as the reference images. The staff should read as useful equipment owned by a traveling alchemist, NOT a heroic weapon, even though the surrounding craftsmanship is beautiful. Full object comfortably contained in a square irregular vignette, soft outer edges dissolve into untouched pale warm ivory paper (#eee7d8); highly detailed center, generous margins.
